main.claim: Open Keyboard Test and press a key: it lights up on the on-screen keyboard and stays marked once tested. A counter shows how many keys you have tested, and Reset clears the marks so you can test again.

sections.heading: How to test your keyboard
sections.body:
Open Keyboard Test in a web browser. The page shows an on-screen keyboard with letters, numbers, F-keys, modifier keys, arrow keys and, on wider screens, a numpad. There is nothing to install.

1. Open [Keyboard Test](https://keyboard-test.lazur.app/).
2. Press a key on your keyboard.
3. Watch the matching key light up on the screen.
4. Keep going until every key you use has lit up.

**A key lights up while you press it, and it stays marked once you have tested it.** The marks are your record, so you can see at a glance which keys have reached the page and which have not.

sections.heading: What the page shows for each press
sections.body:
A panel shows the last key you pressed, with three values: the key, the code and the keyCode. The key is the character or name the browser reports, such as the letter a or Enter. The code names the physical position of the key, such as KeyA. The keyCode is an older number for the same key.

Use the code when you want to know which physical key sent the press. The key value changes with Shift and other modifier keys, but the code does not.

The counter shows how many keys you have tested so far. Reset clears every mark and sets the counter back to zero, so you can run a clean pass.

sections.heading: Keys a web page cannot see
sections.body:
Some keys never reach a web page, because your computer takes them first. The Windows key, the volume keys and the Fn key are in that group. The test cannot light them up or mark them.

So a key that stays dark may be one of these, not a broken key. Press it and see what your computer does instead. If the computer responds, the key works and the page is simply not the place to check it.

sections.heading: When a key stays dark
sections.body:
Press the key firmly, then press it again. Next, open a text box, such as a note or a search bar, and press the key there. If it types or responds in the text box, the key works. The problem is then either a key from the list above or the test itself.

If the key does nothing in any app, the key or its connection may have a problem. Check the connection first. If the key still does nothing, the keyboard may need a repair or a replacement.

sections.heading: Mac and laptop pages
sections.body: Using a MacBook? The [MacBook keyboard test](https://keyboard-test.lazur.app/macbook) covers the Mac keys and Apple's Keyboard Viewer. On a laptop, the [laptop keyboard test](https://keyboard-test.lazur.app/laptop) explains the keys a browser cannot see and what the test does not measure.

pages.title: Keyboard Test for MacBook: Check Every Key Online | Lazur
pages.description: Test every key on your MacBook in the browser. Each key lights up as you press it and stays marked once tested. Reset clears the marks so you can test again.
pages.claim: Open the keyboard test on your MacBook and press each key. The key lights up on the on-screen keyboard and stays marked once tested, and a counter shows how many keys you have covered. The Fn key and volume keys never reach a web page.

sections.heading: How to test every key on a MacBook
sections.body:
Open the keyboard test in your browser on the MacBook, then press each key you want to check. Nothing needs to be installed. The key you press lights up on the on-screen keyboard, and it keeps its mark after you let go.

1. Open the [MacBook keyboard test](https://keyboard-test.lazur.app/macbook) in your browser.
2. Press a letter, then a number.
3. Press each modifier key on the keyboard.
4. Work across the function keys and the arrow keys.
5. Watch the counter. It shows how many keys you have tested.

**A key that stays unmarked after several presses is the one to check.** Press it firmly again, then try it in a text box. The steps for that case are in the section on keys that stay dark.

sections.heading: Reading the on-screen keyboard
sections.body:
The page draws letters, numbers, F-keys, modifier keys and arrow keys. A numpad appears only on wider screens, so a MacBook screen may not show one. Each key lights up while you hold it down. When you release it, the mark stays, so you can see the keys you have covered as you go.

The panel for the last key you pressed shows three values: the key, the code and the keyCode. Use the key for the character or name the browser reports. Use the code for the physical position of the key on the keyboard. The keyCode is an older number for the same key.

Reset clears every mark and sets the counter back to zero. Use it when you want to start a fresh pass, for example after you have tested a few keys by mistake.

sections.heading: Keys a MacBook test cannot show
sections.body:
Some keys never reach a web page at all. On a MacBook that group includes the Fn key and the volume keys. The test cannot light them up or mark them, so a dark key here may still work.

Check these keys another way. Press Fn and watch what your Mac does. Press each volume key and listen for the change in sound. If your Mac responds, the key works, even though the test cannot show it.

sections.heading: See which character each key types
sections.body:
If you want to see the layout your Mac uses, Apple's Keyboard Viewer draws the keys and the characters they type. Click the Input menu in the menu bar, then choose Show Keyboard Viewer.

If you don't see the Input menu, choose Apple menu > System Settings, click Keyboard in the sidebar, then under Text Input click Edit and turn on Show Input menu in menu bar. The steps come from [Apple's Keyboard Viewer guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/use-the-keyboard-viewer-on-mac-mchlp1015/mac).

sections.heading: When a MacBook key stays dark
sections.body:
Press the key firmly, then press it again. Open a text box, such as a note, and press the key there. If it types or does something in the text box, the key works. That points to a key from the list above, or to a problem with the test rather than the key.

If the key does nothing in any app, the key may have a problem. Take the MacBook to a repair service before you assume the worst.

If you want to talk instead of type on your Mac, Lazur is a Mac app: hold two keys and talk, and it types, answers or does the task in any app. Windows is coming, and you can read more at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

faq.q: How do I check my MacBook keyboard?
faq.a: Open the keyboard test on your MacBook and press each key once. Each key lights up while you press it and stays marked after that. Any key still unmarked after several presses is the one to check.

faq.q: Can I test a Mac keyboard online?
faq.a: Yes. The test runs in a web browser, so you do not need to install an app. It draws the keys on screen and marks each one you press. The Fn key and the volume keys never reach a web page, so the test cannot mark them.

faq.q: Why doesn't the Fn key light up?
faq.a: Web pages never receive the Fn key, so the test cannot light it up. Check Fn another way: press it and watch what your Mac does. The Fn key may trigger a function or a shortcut, and that response shows the key works.

faq.q: How do I show the Keyboard Viewer on a Mac?
faq.a: Click the Input menu in the menu bar, then choose Show Keyboard Viewer. If you don't see the Input menu, open Apple menu > System Settings, click Keyboard, then under Text Input click Edit and turn on Show Input menu in menu bar.

pages.title: Keyboard Test Online for Laptop: Check Every Key | Lazur
pages.description: Test a laptop keyboard online in your browser. Press each key and watch it light up on the on-screen keyboard. A counter shows the keys you have tested so far.
pages.claim: Open the keyboard test on your laptop and press keys one at a time. Each key lights up on the on-screen keyboard while you press it and stays marked once tested. Use Reset to clear the marks and test again.

sections.heading: How to test a laptop keyboard online
sections.body:
Open the test in your browser on the laptop, then press each key on the laptop keyboard. You do not need to install anything. The test runs in the browser.

1. Open the [laptop keyboard test](https://keyboard-test.lazur.app/laptop) in your browser.
2. Press a key on the laptop keyboard.
3. Watch the matching key light up on the screen.
4. Keep pressing until the keys you use are marked.
5. Press Reset to clear the marks, then test again for a clean pass.

**The key stays marked after you press it.** So the marks show you which keys have reached the page, and the counter shows how many you have tested.

sections.heading: What each key on screen tells you
sections.body:
While you hold a key down, the matching key on screen lights up. When you let go, the key keeps its mark. The on-screen keyboard includes letters, numbers, F-keys, modifier keys, arrow keys and, on wider screens, a numpad.

The panel for the last key you pressed shows the key, the code and the keyCode. The key is the character or name the browser reports. The code is the physical position of the key, such as KeyA. The keyCode is an older number for the same key.

The counter shows how many keys you have tested. When a key you expect to work stays unmarked, look at the last-key panel first. If it shows nothing for that key, the press did not reach the page.

sections.heading: Keys a laptop test cannot show
sections.body:
Some keys never reach a web page. On a laptop these are usually the Fn key, the Windows key and the volume keys. They are the keys most likely to stay dark when you test a laptop.

To check them, press each one and see what the laptop does. The key works if the laptop responds. The test cannot mark these keys, so a dark key in this group is not proof of a fault.

sections.heading: Reset and test again
sections.body:
Reset clears every mark and sets the counter back to zero. Use it before a new pass so you can see which keys stay unmarked this time.

If a key feels loose or sticky, press it several times in a row, then try the same presses in a text box. The test marks a key once, so it does not show each press. A text box shows whether every press types.

sections.heading: What this test does not measure
sections.body:
This test shows which key presses reach the browser. It does not measure polling rate, typing speed or key response time, and it does not run a hardware diagnostic. It also does not check a touchpad or a touchscreen.

If a key stays unmarked, try it in a text box. If it types there, the key works, and the test is either missing that key or has a problem. If it does nothing in any app, the key or its connection may need a repair.

faq.q: How do I test my laptop keyboard?
faq.a: Open the laptop keyboard test and press each key once. Keys light up as you press them and stay marked, and the counter shows how many you have tested. A key that stays dark is worth a check in a text box.

faq.q: Can I test my laptop keyboard polling rate online?
faq.a: No. This test shows which key presses reach the browser and marks each one you press. It does not measure polling rate, typing speed or response time, so use a tool built for that if you need a rate.

faq.q: How do I run a keyboard diagnostic on a laptop?
faq.a: This page is not a hardware diagnostic. It checks key presses in your browser: a key lights up when the page receives it. If a key stays dark, press it again and try it in a text box. If it types there, the key works.

faq.q: Is there a keyboard tester I can use on a laptop without an app?
faq.a: Yes. The keyboard test runs in your browser, so there is no app to install. It lights up each key you press and keeps a count of the keys you have tested. Reset clears the marks whenever you want to start again.
